_doc: The San Diego freeway network (ONE-CHAIN §4 row 8; Kevin 2026-10-28: 'Yes spin an agent to rebuild'). WHERE EVERY VALUE CAME FROM: this file is doooom-fast/k10-san-diego (archived) project_freeway_net/track.config.json at that repo's HEAD 64161fc (2026-07-28, engine pin .engine-version v0.66.3) -- the project its scripts/build_network.sh built and the config whose slug (san_diego_freeway) and version (0.5.0) are the shipped san_diego_freeway_v0.5.0.zip's (tools/pack_release.py FREEWAY_FILES names san_diego_freeway.kn5; release/NOTES-v0.23.0.md: 'carried forward unchanged from v0.21.0'). The engine copy projects/san-diego-freeway-loop/track.config.json (slug san_diego_freeway_loop, registry engine_projects 'stale duplicate') carries the same source, network, scenery, location and layouts values (JSON-equal) but no lighting.model_yaw_deg, and mirror_x true / true_north 180 -- the frame k10-san-diego's CLAUDE.md says the shipped network was NOT built in ('The freeway network MUST be built mirror_x=false'); its source/ is identical to project_freeway_net's. Values changed from project_freeway_net, each by a named rule: name, ui_series, install_folder, layouts[0].name, author (below, *_doc keys). Nothing else changed; no road, width or elevation is invented here (fleet/LAWS.md L1): the route is the OSM network source declares.
name: San Diego Freeway Free Roam
_name_doc: Kevin's rule for street networks (ledger 0054, docs/ONE-CHAIN.md §3): the open network is '<Area> Free Roam'. The shipped name was 'K10 - San Diego — Freeway' (series + 'Freeway'), so <Area> is the freeway; the public title carries the place because it is read outside Content Manager too (release notes, the zip). In Content Manager the installed name is ship.json ui_name_prefix + layouts[0].name = 'doooom San Diego — Freeway Free Roam', the shape of 'Lake Murray Free Roam'. Kevin's call to change.
_ui_series_doc: Kevin 2026-10-28: 'K10 is gone. doooom.' (docs/ONE-CHAIN.md §3: ui_series = 'doooom <Region>'). project_freeway_net had '' because its name carried 'K10 - San Diego'.
_slug_doc: project_freeway_net's slug, the shipped kn5's name (san_diego_freeway.kn5) and the installed folder that exists (content/tracks/san_diego_freeway, tools/pack_release.py --freeway default); it is also this folder's name with '_' (ONE-CHAIN §3), so nothing is renamed.
_install_folder_doc: ONE-CHAIN §3: install_folder = the slug, no suffixes. tools/ship_track.sh installs under content/tracks/<install_folder> and parks the previous install (the shipped 0.5.0) in the archive.
_version_doc: project_freeway_net's, = the shipped zip. ONE-CHAIN §3: versions keep counting, never reset; the chain's first ship of this track is 0.6.0 and says 'chain' in its notes. Not bumped here: nothing has been built through the chain yet.
author: airoso
_author_doc: project_freeway_net said 'k10-san-diego' (a retired repo, docs/ONE-CHAIN.md §3 'Generations: not a name'); airoso as Milford's.
_about: A drivable FREEROAM loop of San Diego's central freeway box, built straight from OpenStreetMap: I-5 (west leg) -> SR-52 (north leg) -> SR-163 (east leg) -> I-8 (south leg), closed at the four stack interchanges. BOTH directional carriageways plus EVERY on/off ramp and interchange connector (cloverleaf/direct N<->S) come across as separate OSM motorway_link ways. Real USGS 3DEP terrain, physical concrete barrier WALLS along every freeway edge so you can't fly off into the desert, Mission Bay + the Pacific as water. Desert-themed dry ground (no green, no palms).

location._anchor: I-8 in Mission Valley (straight WB stretch near the SR-163 stack) - AC_START snaps to the nearest freeway edge here. (project_freeway_net's spawn rule, build_network_mesh._freeroam_dummies. Since 2026-11-01 the chain's network_reference step replaces that dummies.json: the grid at the START of network.reference_line, AC_TIME_0 at its finish, fleet/LAWS.md L11; lat/lon here still feed the lighting.)

source._doc: osm-network = fetch every drivable way of the listed highway classes inside bbox straight from Overpass, then node-snap them into one connected road GRAPH (scripts/gps/network.py). No KML. bbox is (south, west, north, east). motorway + motorway_link gives the 4 freeways, both carriageways, and every ramp/interchange connector in the box.
source._refs_doc: Mainline carriageways are restricted to these exact OSM refs so I-805 (which threads the same box and CROSSES CA-163) is excluded. Ramps/links are kept regardless, then network.keep_largest_component prunes I-805's now-orphaned ramps.

network._doc: Graph-build knobs (scripts/gps/network.py). snap_grid kept SMALL so the two ~20 m-apart directional carriageways stay separate edges while coincident OSM ramp/mainline nodes still merge.
network._stable_snap_doc: Ledger 0075 (2026-11-03, the Mac agent): build_network's greedy snap moves a cluster's centre by a running mean as points join it, so a node two OSM ways share, met again in a later way, could land in a different cluster: the ways then ended at two nodes 2-9 m apart with no link (101 such pairs in this network, three of them holes in I 8 eastbound at 33, 3,373 and 3,914 m, read as ground on top mid-lane and severe steps). true maps every point to its nearest FINAL cluster centre after all are assigned, and every edge that ends at a node ends at its seed point (scripts.gps.network._NodeGrid.nearest): one coordinate, one node. A node's point can then be a ramp's vertex at a gore, so classify's travel vote (only) reads an edge's interior samples, or a short edge's middle vertex (an 18.7 m I 8 piece otherwise came out undecided and network_reference refused the line).
network._join_nodes_doc: Ledger 0075: ONE height per shared node (scripts.geometry.network_joins). network_elev smoothed and forward-capped each edge alone, so 334 of 365 shared nodes met at two heights (169 by more than 0.5 m, worst 19.86 m); build_network_mesh laid each edge's OSM-layer deck lift alone, so a flyover's lift ended at its edge boundary (the 3.3-4.1 m surface steps at 1,373 and 7,036 m) and a ramp could start at full layer height beside an at-grade mainline. true pins each node to its THROUGH pair's mean (two mainline ends running on straightest; ramps take the mainline's value), at grade in network_elev (both ends pinned within the 5 % cap) and for the deck lift in build_network_mesh (ramped back, then the deck's 6.5 % cap with both ends held).

reference_line._doc: THE LINE THE SHIP PHASE WALKS (scripts.geometry.network_reference, the draft step network_reference; Kevin 2026-11-01: 'a complete track list installed by morning'). A network has no single centreline, and the prep / write_ai_line / make_map / verify_kn5 / drive_test read one (tracks/san-diego-freeway/README.md 'What the Windows run owes'). This declares ONE real mainline, never an invented one (fleet/LAWS.md L1): Interstate 8 eastbound, end to end inside source.bbox, chosen from the draft's OWN edges at draft time. ref 'I 8' is one of source.refs, the OSM ref tag scripts.gps.classify writes as a motorway edge's name; eastbound = the carriageway whose OSM ways are drawn west to east (classify travel_dir, recorded because this block exists), the right-hand one of the pair (checked: where I 8 westbound runs within 80 m it must lie on the line's left). The resolver takes the longest directed chain of non-ramp I 8 edges that continue each other at a shared node (no joint turning > max_joint_turn_deg); every point of the line is a vertex of a built edge. Edge ids are not written here: they are the draft's own and change with every net step on live OSM (the README: no snapshot of the July OSM exists); edge_ids may pin a list once a draft is read. Everything else the network builds (I 8 westbound, I 5, CA 52, CA 163, every ramp and connector) is in track.obj and the kn5 but walked by no line gate: data/network.reference.json lists it by id and name, drive_test prints it, ship.json _owed names the hole.
reference_line._bridge_max_edges_doc: [invented] At most 2 non-ramp freeway edges of ANOTHER name may sit INSIDE the chain (never at its ends; each named in network.reference.json 'bridged'): classify names a mainline piece by a nearest-way vote every 25 m, and a short I 8 piece passing under the CA 163 or I 5 stack can lose that vote. Only non-ramp freeway edges can bridge (OSM tags freeway-to-freeway connectors motorway_link, which classify makes ramps), only between two I 8 eastbound edges (the chain starts and ends on I 8), and only through joints turning <= max_joint_turn_deg. 0 = refuse instead.

_mirror_x_doc: project_freeway_net's (k10-san-diego CLAUDE.md: built unmirrored so it shares the Lake Murray loop's frame). The projects/ copy's true is the stale part of that copy.

scenery._doc: Desert dressing. dry_only kills irrigated green (all dry chaparral/dirt); palms off. Physical WALLS replace the visual guardrail; gantries stay for freeway feel.
scenery._chain_doc: Carried over as shipped. What the chain's draft READS of this block: walls, viaduct, dry_only, ocean (scripts.geometry.build_network_mesh) and terrain.bbox_swne (scripts.elevation.network_elev). Everything else here (corridor_margin_m, palms, streetlights, tree_*, bush_*, light_spacing_m, freeway_furniture, water_bodies, buildings) was read only by scripts.environment.build_network_env, which the chain never runs (no generated furniture: ONE-CHAIN §2 row 2) -- inert, kept as the record of what 0.5.0 shipped with. Gantries, Mission Bay's water and the rest are authoring items now.

walls._doc: Physical concrete barrier along both edges of every freeway-class edge (build_network_mesh -> 1WALL_*). height_m tall enough to stop a launched car; offset_m past the shoulder outer lip.
walls._seat_doc: Ledger 0075. offset_m 3.2 -> 0.5 (PC experiment 1) put the at-grade barrier on the 3 m graded shoulder. seat 'seated' (build_network_mesh._wall_seated, Mac 2026-11-03) stands every column on a surface: on a deck (the network's own viaduct lift >= 1 m, or a span the mesh already builds slab + piers under) on a 1 m 1KERB_deckedge slab beyond the pavement, 0.7 m out; at grade offset_m out with its base 0.5 m under the BUILT ground; gapped (and the slab clipped) wherever another edge's pavement lies under it (merges, gores, ramp tapers), triangle-exact as audit D reads it; following the ribbon's own width. The default seat 'deck' is the old sweep, byte for byte.

viaduct._doc: Real 3DEP carries the terrain grades; OSM bridge LAYER tags carry the flyovers. So the synthetic dip-bridge is OFF (max_lift_m 0) - only layer_height_m raises OSM-tagged flyover decks so interchanges grade-separate.

terrain._doc: Override the DEM bbox to reach WEST past I-5 over Mission Bay to the coast, so the bay + ocean have ground under them.
terrain._east_doc: Ledger 0075 (2026-11-03): east -117.125 -> -117.115. The network's edges run to -117.1224 (CA 163 / I 8 east of the box; network.geojson), 250 m past the old grid, so the 800 m skirt apron lay over their pavement (audit J 14-23, worst 800 m) and their barriers stood over the skirt (drive_test floating furniture 5 after the seated barrier). -117.115 covers every edge plus ~690 m.

ocean._doc: Pacific to the true WEST: carve terrain west of lon_from below sea level + a flat sea-level plane out to lon_to.

water_bodies._doc: Mission Bay - the big water body just WEST of I-5 between I-8 and SR-52.

_true_north_doc: project_freeway_net's; build_network_mesh writes it back (resolve_true_north: 0 for an unmirrored frame).

layouts.name: Freeway Free Roam
layouts._doc: Single freeroam layout over the whole freeway network. AC_START on I-8 near the SR-163 stack. Drive the loop either direction; every ramp is open.
layouts._id_doc: id 'freeroam' is project_freeway_net's, kept (ONE-CHAIN §3: 'Ids stay stable so setups survive'); name per Kevin's '<Area> Free Roam'. No race layout: a network is Free Roam only.
